name: Cylinder block
what: The heavy cast metal body of the engine that holds the cylinders and carries the crankshaft.
does: Forms the backbone every other engine part bolts to and contains the coolant and oil passages.
lookFor: Check the deck for flatness and the casting for cracks, especially between cylinders and around bolt holes.

name: Cylinder liners
what: Hard iron sleeves cast into the block that form the walls the pistons slide in.
does: Give the piston rings a tough, round surface to seal against.
lookFor: Measure bore diameter, taper and out-of-round, and look for vertical scoring or a ridge at the top of ring travel.

name: Main bearing caps
what: Heavy metal caps that bolt to the bottom of the block around each crankshaft journal.
does: Clamp the main bearings and hold the crankshaft in the block.
lookFor: Keep each cap in its original position and direction, and check the bearing saddles for fretting or spun-bearing marks.

name: Cylinder head
what: The cast metal lid on top of the cylinders that holds the valves, ports and often the camshafts.
does: Closes off the combustion chambers and controls air in and exhaust out through its valves.
lookFor: Check the deck face for warp with a straightedge and look for cracks between valve seats and around coolant passages.

name: Crankshaft
what: A long, heavy shaft with offset journals that runs the length of the engine.
does: Turns the up-and-down push of the pistons into rotation that drives the transmission.
lookFor: Measure journal diameters for wear and taper, check runout, and look for scoring, heat marks or cracks at the journal edges.

name: Main bearings
what: Thin, curved half-shell bearings that sit between the block and the crankshaft journals.
does: Let the crankshaft spin on a film of pressurized oil without metal-to-metal contact.
lookFor: Look for scoring, embedded debris, copper showing through and uneven wear, and measure oil clearance.

name: Crankshaft thrust washers
what: Flat half-moon washers fitted at one main journal of the crankshaft.
does: Stop the crankshaft from sliding forward and back along its own length.
lookFor: Measure crankshaft end play and check the thrust faces for scoring or uneven wear.

name: Pistons
what: Cylindrical metal plugs that slide up and down inside each cylinder.
does: Take the force of combustion and push the connecting rods to turn the crankshaft.
lookFor: Check skirts for scuffing, crowns for burning or cracks, and ring grooves for wear, and measure piston-to-bore clearance.

name: Piston rings
what: Thin split metal rings that sit in grooves around each piston.
does: Seal combustion pressure above the piston and scrape extra oil off the cylinder wall.
lookFor: Measure end gap in the bore and side clearance in the groove, and note which side faces up before fitting.

name: Piston pins
what: Short hardened steel tubes, held in by clips, that pass through the piston and the top of the connecting rod.
does: Let the connecting rod pivot under the piston as the crankshaft turns.
lookFor: Check for scoring or a step worn into the pin, and fit new circlips.

name: Connecting rods
what: Strong steel links with a small eye at the top and a split big end at the bottom.
does: Connect each piston to the crankshaft and carry the combustion force between them.
lookFor: Check for bend and twist, check that the big-end bore is round, and keep each cap with its own rod.

name: Connecting rod bearings
what: Thin half-shell bearings fitted inside the big end of each connecting rod.
does: Let the rod turn on its crankshaft journal on a film of oil.
lookFor: Look for scoring, smeared lining and embedded debris, and measure oil clearance.

name: Small-end bushings
what: Pressed-in bronze sleeves in the small top eye of each connecting rod.
does: Give the piston pin a smooth, replaceable surface to pivot in.
lookFor: Measure pin-to-bushing clearance and look for looseness or scoring in the bore.

name: Drive plate (flexplate)
what: A thin steel disc with a toothed ring gear that bolts to the back of the crankshaft on automatic cars.
does: Connects the crankshaft to the torque converter and gives the starter motor teeth to turn.
lookFor: Look for cracks around the bolt holes, chipped ring gear teeth, and a bent or damaged sensor ring.

name: Crankshaft pulley
what: A grooved wheel, often with a rubber-mounted damper ring, on the front end of the crankshaft.
does: Drives the accessory belt and, when it has a damper, soaks up twisting vibration in the crankshaft.
lookFor: Check the rubber layer for cracks or slipping and the seal surface on the hub for a worn groove.

name: Balance shafts
what: A pair of weighted shafts, driven by gears from the crankshaft, that spin alongside it.
does: Cancel the shaking forces an inline four makes so the engine runs smoother.
lookFor: Check bearing journals and drive gear teeth for wear, and line up the timing marks exactly on reassembly.

name: Intake and exhaust valves
what: Mushroom-shaped metal plugs on long stems that open and close the ports in the cylinder head.
does: Let air into and exhaust out of each cylinder at the right moment, then seal it for compression.
lookFor: Check faces for burning or pitting, stems for wear and bend, and the thickness of the edge around the head.

name: Valve springs and retainers
what: Coil springs held on each valve stem by a cap and two small split keepers.
does: Snap each valve shut and keep it following the camshaft at high speed.
lookFor: Measure free length and squareness, check spring pressure, and look for cracked retainers or worn keepers.

name: Valve guides
what: Thin tubes pressed into the cylinder head that each valve stem slides through.
does: Keep the valve centered on its seat and carry heat away from the stem.
lookFor: Measure stem-to-guide clearance and check for wear that has flared the ends of the bore.

name: Valve seats
what: Hardened rings set into the cylinder head where each valve closes.
does: Give the valve face a tight, heat-resistant surface to seal against.
lookFor: Check contact width and position, and look for pitting, burning, cracks or a seat that has sunk.

name: Valve stem seals
what: Small rubber caps that fit over the top of each valve guide.
does: Stop oil running down the valve stems into the ports and cylinders.
lookFor: Replace them on every rebuild, and press each one on squarely without tearing the lip.

name: Valve shims
what: Small hardened discs, made in graded thicknesses, that sit between the camshaft and each valve.
does: Set the gap, called valve clearance, between the camshaft and each valve.
lookFor: Measure clearances before teardown, and record each shim thickness so you can work out replacements.

name: Roller finger followers
what: Short steel levers with a small roller in the middle that ride under the camshaft lobes.
does: Pass the lift of each cam lobe to its valve with very little friction.
lookFor: Check the roller for flat spots, pitting or play, and the pads at each end for wear.

name: Hydraulic lash adjusters
what: Small oil-filled plungers in the head that one end of each follower pivots on.
does: Take up slack in the valvetrain automatically, so the valves never need manual adjustment.
lookFor: Check for scoring, sticking or a spongy feel, and keep them upright and full of oil before fitting.

name: Camshaft carrier
what: A machined frame or housing that bolts to the top of the cylinder head and holds the camshafts.
does: Supports the camshafts in their bearings at the right height and alignment over the valves.
lookFor: Check bearing bores for scoring and the sealing faces for flatness and old sealant.

name: Camshafts
what: Shafts with egg-shaped lobes along their length, driven from the crankshaft.
does: Open each valve by the right amount at the right time as the lobes turn.
lookFor: Check lobes for pitting or flat wear and journals for scoring, and measure runout and end play.

name: Camshaft bearing caps
what: Small machined caps that bolt over each camshaft journal.
does: Clamp the camshafts in their bearings while letting them turn.
lookFor: Keep every cap in its original place and direction, and check the bearing surfaces for scoring.

name: Rocker cover
what: The cover bolted on top of the cylinder head over the camshafts, also called a valve cover.
does: Keeps oil in and dirt out of the valvetrain.
lookFor: Check the gasket groove and sealing face for warp or cracks, and fit a new gasket.

name: CVVL intake lift unit
what: An oil-filled electrohydraulic unit on the cylinder head that sits between the intake camshaft and the intake valves.
does: Varies how far and how long the intake valves open, so the engine can control airflow with less use of the throttle.
lookFor: Handle it as a sealed assembly, keep it clean and primed with oil, and check its oil feed seals.

name: Cam phasers
what: Oil-driven hubs on the ends of the camshafts that also carry the timing sprockets.
does: Turn each camshaft slightly ahead of or behind the crankshaft to change valve timing while the engine runs.
lookFor: Check that each locking pin engages and each rotor moves freely, and look for worn sprocket teeth.

name: Timing chains
what: Metal link chains that loop around sprockets on the crankshaft and camshafts.
does: Keep the camshafts turning in exact step with the crankshaft.
lookFor: Measure chain stretch over a set number of links and look for stiff links or worn pins.

name: Timing sprockets
what: Toothed wheels on the crankshaft or an idler shaft that a timing chain wraps around.
does: Pass drive between the crankshaft, the chains and the camshafts.
lookFor: Check teeth for hooked or sharpened wear and the key or mating face for damage.

name: Chain tensioners
what: Spring and oil-pressure plungers, usually pushing on a pivoting arm, that press against a timing chain.
does: Keep the chain tight as it wears and damp out slack when engine speed changes.
lookFor: Check each plunger for scoring and free movement and each arm face for grooves, and lock them retracted before fitting.

name: Timing chain guides
what: Rigid rails with a plastic wear face that a timing chain slides along.
does: Hold the chain on its path and stop it slapping.
lookFor: Look for deep grooves, cracks or missing pieces of the plastic face.

name: Timing covers
what: Cast covers that close in the timing chains at one end of the engine.
does: Keep oil in around the chain drive and often carry seals, pumps or mounts.
lookFor: Check the sealing faces for corrosion or damage and clean off all old sealant before refitting.

name: Engine oil pan
what: The pan bolted to the bottom of the engine that holds the oil supply, sometimes in an upper and a lower section.
does: Stores the engine oil and collects it as it drains back from the parts above.
lookFor: Check for dents that reach the pickup, cracks and damaged drain threads, and clean the sealing faces.

name: Oil pickup and strainer
what: A pipe with a mesh screen on the end that dips into the oil in the pan.
does: Feeds oil to the pump while keeping large debris out.
lookFor: Clear the screen of sludge or debris and replace the seal where the pipe meets the pump or block.

name: Engine oil pump
what: A gear, rotor or vane pump driven by the crankshaft or a chain.
does: Pushes oil under pressure to the bearings, camshafts and other moving parts.
lookFor: Measure rotor or vane clearances, check the housing for scoring, and make sure the relief valve moves freely.

name: Oil filters and screens
what: Paper filter elements, or small fine mesh screens, set into the oil passages.
does: Catch dirt and metal particles before the oil reaches parts with tight clearances.
lookFor: Replace the element, clean or replace any screens, and look in the old filter for metal flakes.

name: Oil cooler
what: A small heat exchanger that passes engine oil close to coolant.
does: Pulls heat out of the oil so it does not thin out or break down.
lookFor: Flush it well after any internal failure, check for leaks between oil and coolant, and fit new seals.

name: Oil baffles and windage trays
what: Shaped metal or plastic plates that sit close to spinning parts or across an oil or fluid pan.
does: Keep oil from sloshing away from the pickup and from being whipped up by moving parts.
lookFor: Check for cracks, loose mounting points and rub marks from parts that have touched them.

name: Crankcase oil separator
what: A box or cover with baffles inside, placed in the path of the crankcase ventilation gases.
does: Strips oil mist out of crankcase gases before they are drawn back into the intake.
lookFor: Check for blocked passages, cracked housings and leaking seals.

name: Piston cooling oil jets
what: Small nozzles in the bottom of the block aimed up at the underside of each piston.
does: Spray oil under the pistons to cool them and lubricate the piston pins.
lookFor: Make sure each jet is straight, clear and aimed correctly, because a bent jet can hit a piston or rod.

name: Pump drive chains
what: Short chains with their sprockets that drive an oil or fluid pump mounted off to one side.
does: Turn the pump whenever the engine or the torque converter is turning.
lookFor: Check for stretch, worn sprocket teeth and stiff or noisy links.

name: Water pump
what: An impeller pump, driven by a belt or chain, mounted on the engine.
does: Circulates coolant through the engine and radiator.
lookFor: Check for bearing play, weeping from the weep hole and corroded or broken impeller blades.

name: Thermostat and housing
what: A wax-pellet valve that sits in a housing in the coolant path.
does: Keeps coolant in the engine until it warms up, then opens to send it to the radiator.
lookFor: Replace it on a rebuild, and check the housing for cracks and the sealing face for corrosion.

name: Coolant pipes and hoses
what: Metal pipes, rubber hoses and tanks that carry coolant around the engine.
does: Route coolant between the pump, block, heads, heater and radiator.
lookFor: Look for cracked or soft hoses and corroded pipe ends, and fit new O-rings.

name: Water jacket spacer
what: A shaped plastic insert that sits in the coolant passage around the cylinders.
does: Steers coolant flow so the cylinder walls warm up evenly.
lookFor: Check for cracks or warping and fit it the right way round.

name: Intake manifold and throttle body
what: A set of tubes or a plastic box that bolts to the head, with the throttle valve at its inlet.
does: Meters air through the throttle and shares it evenly between the cylinders.
lookFor: Check the runner gaskets, clean carbon off the throttle plate, and look for cracks in plastic sections.

name: Tumble generator valves
what: Small flaps inside the intake runners near the head, moved by an electric actuator.
does: Partly close at low load so incoming air tumbles, which helps the fuel burn cleanly when cold.
lookFor: Check the flaps for free movement and the shafts for play or sticking carbon.

name: Fuel injectors
what: Electrically opened nozzles that spray fuel either into the intake port or straight into the cylinder.
does: Deliver a measured spray of fuel for each combustion cycle.
lookFor: Fit new seals and O-rings, keep the tips clean, and use new combustion seals on direct injectors.

name: Fuel rail
what: A metal tube that the fuel injectors plug into.
does: Holds fuel under pressure and feeds it to each injector.
lookFor: Check the fittings for damage, cap the openings against dirt, and use new seals where the injectors fit.

name: High-pressure fuel lines
what: Rigid steel pipes with machined end fittings that leave the high-pressure fuel pump.
does: Carry fuel at very high pressure from the pump to the fuel rail.
lookFor: Use new lines if the maker calls for them, and check the cone-shaped ends for marks or deformation.

name: High-pressure fuel pump
what: A plunger pump mounted on the head, pushed by a camshaft lobe through a roller tappet.
does: Raises fuel to the very high pressure that direct injection needs.
lookFor: Check the tappet roller and the cam lobe that drives it for wear, and fit new seals.

name: EGR pipe
what: A metal pipe that links the exhaust side of the engine to the intake side.
does: Carries a little exhaust gas back into the intake to lower combustion temperatures and emissions.
lookFor: Check for carbon blockage, cracks and damaged flange gaskets.

name: PCV valve
what: A small one-way valve in the crankcase ventilation line.
does: Lets crankcase gases be drawn into the intake while blocking flow the other way.
lookFor: Shake it to hear the check ball move, and replace it if it sticks or is gummed up.

name: Turbocharger
what: An exhaust-driven turbine wheel joined by a shaft to an air compressor wheel.
does: Uses exhaust energy to pack more air into the engine for more power.
lookFor: Check shaft play, look for chipped or rubbing wheel blades, and check for oil in the inlet or outlet.

name: Turbo oil feed and return lines
what: Small metal pipes that bring oil to the turbocharger bearings and drain it back to the pan.
does: Keep the turbocharger shaft oiled and cooled.
lookFor: Fit new lines or at least new sealing washers, and make sure no debris or sealant can reach the turbo.

name: Heat shields
what: Formed metal covers that sit over or around hot exhaust parts.
does: Protect nearby wiring, hoses and plastic parts from exhaust heat.
lookFor: Check for cracks, broken mounts and missing fasteners that would let them rattle.

name: Head gasket
what: A thin layered steel sheet cut to the shape of the top of the block.
does: Seals combustion pressure, coolant and oil between the block and the cylinder head.
lookFor: Always fit a new one, and make sure both faces are clean, flat and dry.

name: Head bolts
what: Long high-strength bolts that clamp the cylinder head to the block.
does: Hold the head down hard enough to keep the head gasket sealed under combustion pressure.
lookFor: Use new bolts when they are the stretch type, clean the threaded holes, and follow the tightening sequence.

name: Block joining bolts
what: The large bolts that hold the two halves of a split engine block together.
does: Clamp the block halves, and the main bearings between them, around the crankshaft.
lookFor: Check the threads, follow the tightening sequence, and use new bolts if the maker calls for them.

name: Connecting rod bolts
what: High-strength bolts that hold each connecting rod cap to its rod.
does: Clamp the rod cap tightly around the rod bearing at high engine speed.
lookFor: Replace them when they are the stretch type, and tighten them in stages to the specified torque and angle.

name: Crankshaft oil seals
what: Rubber lip seals pressed into the covers at each end of the crankshaft.
does: Keep oil inside the engine where the crankshaft passes out of it.
lookFor: Fit new seals squarely to the right depth, and check the crankshaft surface for a groove worn by the old lip.

name: Converter hub seals
what: Lip seals and sealing rings at the front of the transmission where the torque converter hub and shafts enter.
does: Keep transmission fluid in around the spinning converter hub.
lookFor: Fit new seals and check the converter hub for scoring or a worn groove.

name: Axle seals
what: Lip seals where the drive axles enter the transmission or differential.
does: Keep fluid or gear oil in while the axles turn.
lookFor: Replace them on a rebuild and check the axle surfaces for grooves or nicks.

name: Shaft sealing rings
what: Narrow plastic or cast-iron rings that sit in grooves on shafts and hubs.
does: Seal oil pressure as it passes between a fixed part and a turning one.
lookFor: Replace them, check the grooves and bores for wear, and size new plastic rings before fitting if required.

name: Case gaskets
what: Flat gaskets or formed seals that sit between two sections of a transmission case.
does: Seal fluid in at the joint between case sections and around tubes that cross it.
lookFor: Fit new ones and clean both faces without gouging the aluminum.

name: Gallery, drain and fill plugs
what: Threaded or pressed-in plugs that close off drilled passages, drain holes and fill holes.
does: Seal passages that were drilled during manufacture or are opened only for service.
lookFor: Remove gallery plugs so passages can be cleaned, and fit new sealing washers or O-rings.

name: Wiring harness
what: A bundle of wires, connectors and clips wrapped together as one assembly.
does: Carries power and signals between the control modules and every sensor and actuator.
lookFor: Label connectors before removal, and check for melted insulation, chafed wires and broken clips.

name: Knock sensors
what: Small vibration sensors bolted to the side of the block.
does: Pick up the sharp ping of knock so the engine computer can pull back ignition timing.
lookFor: Tighten each one to its exact torque, because too tight or too loose changes what it hears.

name: Crankshaft position sensor
what: A magnetic sensor aimed at a toothed ring on the crankshaft or drive plate.
does: Tells the engine computer crankshaft speed and position for spark and fuel timing.
lookFor: Check the tip for metal debris or damage and the O-ring for cracks.

name: Camshaft position sensors
what: Magnetic sensors aimed at a toothed target on each camshaft.
does: Tell the engine computer where each camshaft is so it can time injection and check cam timing.
lookFor: Check the tips for metal debris or damage and the O-rings for cracks.

name: Temperature sensors
what: Small threaded or clipped sensors whose electrical resistance changes with temperature.
does: Report coolant or metal temperature to the engine computer.
lookFor: Check connectors for corrosion and fit new sealing washers or O-rings.

name: Oil control solenoids
what: Electrically switched valves that open or close oil passages on command.
does: Let the engine computer steer oil flow, for example to the cam phasers or the piston cooling jets.
lookFor: Clean or replace their inlet screens and check that the plunger or spool moves freely.

name: Ignition coils and spark plugs
what: Coils that sit on top of each spark plug, and the plugs screwed into the head.
does: Make a high-voltage spark in each cylinder to light the fuel and air.
lookFor: Fit new plugs gapped to spec, and check coil boots for cracks or burn tracks.

name: Alternator
what: A belt-driven electrical generator mounted on the engine.
does: Charges the battery and powers the electrics while the engine runs.
lookFor: Spin the pulley to check for a rough or noisy bearing.

name: Speed sensors
what: Small sensors aimed at a toothed or magnetic ring on a transmission shaft or drum.
does: Tell the transmission computer how fast the shafts are turning.
lookFor: Clean metal debris off the tip and check the O-ring and connector.

name: Pressure sensors
what: Small sensors screwed into hydraulic passages.
does: Report fluid pressure so the transmission computer can confirm a clutch has applied.
lookFor: Fit new seals and check the connector pins for damage.

name: Transmission range sensor
what: A switch or sensor on the manual shaft that reads which selector position is chosen.
does: Tells the computers whether the driver picked park, reverse, neutral or drive.
lookFor: Set it to the correct position on reassembly and check the contacts or magnet for damage.

name: Transmission control module
what: An electronic control unit mounted on or near the transmission.
does: Reads sensors and drives the solenoids to choose ratios and control shifts.
lookFor: Keep it clean and dry, and run the adaptation or learning routine after the rebuild.

name: Transmission solenoids
what: Electrically controlled valves that mount on the valve body.
does: Set the hydraulic pressures that apply clutches and move the pulleys.
lookFor: Check their resistance, look for debris on their screens, and fit new O-rings.

name: Converter housing
what: The bell-shaped front section of a transmission case that surrounds the torque converter.
does: Bolts the transmission to the engine and encloses the converter.
lookFor: Check the mating face and dowels, and look for cracks around the mounting points.

name: Transmission case
what: The main aluminum housing that holds the gears, shafts and hydraulics.
does: Holds all the internal parts in alignment and contains the fluid.
lookFor: Check bearing bores and piston bores for wear or scoring, and look for cracks.

name: Extension housing
what: A tail section bolted to the back of the transmission case.
does: Encloses the rear output and supports its shaft and seal.
lookFor: Check the bushing and seal bore for wear and the mating face for damage.

name: Case covers and plates
what: Bolted aluminum or steel covers and plates on a transmission case.
does: Close openings in the case and form some of its internal oil passages.
lookFor: Clean the sealing faces, check for warp, and fit new gaskets or sealant.

name: Valve body cover
what: The cover bolted over the valve body on the side or bottom of the transmission.
does: Encloses the valve body and solenoids and keeps fluid in.
lookFor: Clean the sealing face, check it for warp, and fit a new gasket.

name: Transmission oil pump
what: A vane, gear or rotor pump inside the transmission, driven whenever the engine runs.
does: Makes the fluid pressure that applies clutches, squeezes the pulleys and lubricates the gears.
lookFor: Check vanes or rotors and the housing for scoring, and measure clearances where specified.

name: Valve body
what: A block of maze-like passages and sliding spool valves, often with solenoids attached.
does: Sends pressurized fluid to the right clutches or pulleys to make each ratio.
lookFor: Check the valves for sticking and bore wear, look for debris, and tighten its bolts in the correct order.

name: Transmission filter
what: A filter or mesh strainer that fluid passes through on its way to the pump.
does: Traps clutch material and metal particles before they reach the pump and valve body.
lookFor: Replace it on every rebuild and look in the old one for metal or friction material.

name: Transmission oil pan
what: A shallow pan bolted under the transmission that holds fluid.
does: Stores fluid and usually carries a magnet that catches metal particles.
lookFor: Read the debris on the magnet and pan floor, and check the flange for bends.

name: Fluid lines and tubes
what: Metal tubes and hoses that carry transmission fluid inside or outside the case.
does: Route fluid between the valve body, case passages, cooler and other hydraulic parts.
lookFor: Check for kinks, cracks and trapped debris, and fit new O-rings at each end.

name: Multi-plate clutches
what: Stacks of alternating friction and steel plates inside a drum, squeezed together by a hydraulic piston.
does: Lock two turning parts together when applied, to make a gear ratio.
lookFor: Check friction plates for burning or glazing and steel plates for heat marks, and measure the pack clearance.

name: Multi-plate brakes
what: Stacks of friction and steel plates like a clutch, but splined to the case so they hold instead of turn.
does: Hold part of the gear train still against the case to make a gear ratio.
lookFor: Check friction plates for burning or glazing and steel plates for heat marks, and measure the pack clearance.

name: Dog clutches
what: Pairs of rings with interlocking teeth that a hydraulic piston slides together.
does: Lock two parts solidly with no slip, where a friction clutch would waste energy when open.
lookFor: Check the teeth for rounded or chipped edges and the piston for smooth movement.

name: Planetary gear sets
what: Gear sets with a sun gear in the middle, planet gears on a carrier around it, and a ring gear around the outside.
does: Give different ratios, or reverse, depending on which member is driven and which is held.
lookFor: Check teeth for pitting or chips, planet gears for end play and rough bearings, and thrust washers for wear.

name: Input shaft
what: The shaft that enters the transmission from the torque converter turbine.
does: Carries engine torque into the gear train or the variator.
lookFor: Check splines, bearing journals and sealing ring grooves for wear.

name: Transfer gears
what: Gears on a short shaft that carry drive across from one shaft line to another.
does: Pass output torque over to the differential or toward the rear-wheel drive path.
lookFor: Check teeth for pitting and chips and bearings for roughness or play.

name: Output gear and support
what: The output gear and the bearing support it turns in, at the end of the gear train.
does: Carries the finished output of the gear train toward the transfer gear and differential.
lookFor: Check the gear teeth, the bearing seats and the bearing preload.

name: Selective shims
what: Precision washers made in a range of graded thicknesses.
does: Set end play or bearing preload when shafts and cases go back together.
lookFor: Measure before choosing, keep the old shims labeled by location, and never guess a thickness.

name: Shaft bearings
what: Ball or roller bearings pressed onto shafts or into the case.
does: Support turning shafts with low friction under heavy load.
lookFor: Spin them clean and dry to feel for roughness, and look for pitting or heat discoloration.

name: Manual shaft and linkage
what: The shaft and levers inside the case that the gear selector cable turns.
does: Move the manual valve and the park rod as the driver selects a range.
lookFor: Check the detent spring and lever for wear and the shaft seal for leaks.

name: Parking pawl and rod
what: A hinged steel pawl with a tooth, pushed into place by a rod and cam.
does: Drops into a toothed gear in park to lock the output so the car cannot roll.
lookFor: Check the pawl tooth and park gear for wear and the return spring for strength.

name: Variator pulleys
what: Pairs of cone-shaped steel discs on a shaft, with one half able to slide in and out.
does: Change the diameter the chain runs on, giving the CVT a smooth, stepless range of ratios.
lookFor: Check the cone faces for scoring or a stepped wear track and the sliding half for free movement.

name: Variator chain
what: A heavy steel chain made of many plates and pins that runs between the two variator pulleys.
does: Carries the drive from one pulley to the other while they change ratio.
lookFor: Check the pin ends and plates for wear, cracks and damage.

name: Variator chain guides
what: Plastic guides that ride close to the variator chain between the pulleys.
does: Steady the chain and limit whipping as the ratio changes.
lookFor: Look for deep wear tracks, cracks or broken pieces.

name: Torque converter
what: A large sealed doughnut-shaped housing full of fluid that bolts to the drive plate.
does: Passes engine power to the transmission through fluid, multiplies torque from a stop, and locks up at cruise.
lookFor: Check the hub for scoring, replace or flush it after any internal failure, and make sure it is fully engaged in the pump when fitted.

name: Stator support
what: A fixed hollow shaft that reaches from the front of the transmission into the torque converter.
does: Holds the converter stator still in one direction and carries fluid passages to the converter.
lookFor: Check the splines, bushings and sealing ring grooves for wear.

name: Differential
what: A gear set with a large ring gear on a carrier that holds small side and spider gears.
does: Splits torque between the two front wheels and lets them turn at different speeds in corners.
lookFor: Check gear teeth for pitting and carrier bearings for roughness, and set preload where the maker requires it.

name: Drive pinion
what: A small gear on the end of a shaft that meshes with the differential ring gear.
does: Passes the transmission output to the differential ring gear.
lookFor: Check the tooth contact pattern, bearing preload and pinion depth shims.

name: AWD transfer clutch
what: An electronically controlled multi-plate clutch at the rear of the transmission.
does: Sends a varying share of torque to the rear wheels for all-wheel drive.
lookFor: Check the plates for burning or glazing and the piston and control solenoid for proper operation.

name: Power transfer unit
what: A small gearbox bolted to the side of a front-drive transmission.
does: Turns drive toward the rear prop shaft for all-wheel drive.
lookFor: Check its oil for metal and its seals for leaks.

name: Transmission (complete unit)
what: The whole transmission handled as one unit, separated from or joined to the engine.
does: Changes gear ratios and passes engine power on to the wheels.

name: Engine stand
what: A wheeled steel frame with a rotating head that bolts to the back of an engine.
does: Holds the engine at working height and lets you turn it over during the rebuild.

name: Transmission fluid
what: The specified oil-like fluid that fills an automatic or CVT transmission.
does: Lubricates, cools and carries hydraulic pressure inside the transmission.
lookFor: Note the color, smell and any debris in the old fluid, and refill only with the exact fluid the maker specifies.

name: Gear oil
what: A thick oil made for heavily loaded gear sets.
does: Lubricates the differential gears and bearings.
lookFor: Look for metal particles in the drained oil and refill with the specified grade.

name: Engine cover and NVH pads
what: A plastic cover over the top of the engine plus foam pads and blocks around it.
does: Cut down engine noise and tidy the look of the engine bay.

name: A/C compressor
what: A belt-driven pump for the air conditioning refrigerant.
does: Squeezes refrigerant so the air conditioning can cool the cabin.

name: Accessory drive belt
what: A ribbed rubber belt with a tensioner and idler pulleys.
does: Drives the alternator, compressor and other accessories from the crankshaft pulley.
lookFor: Check the belt for cracks or glazing and the tensioner and idlers for rough or noisy bearings.

name: Engine mounts
what: Rubber-and-metal blocks or brackets that hold the engine in the car.
does: Support the engine and soak up its vibration.
lookFor: Look for cracked, separated or collapsed rubber.
